title: ICSE Class 10 History, Chapter 15: Non-Aligned Movement, Step by Step
subtitle: For students who find history hard. The meaning and features of non-alignment, why newly free nations chose it, Panchsheel, Bandung and the Belgrade summit, the architects of NAM, its objectives and achievements, and Jawaharlal Nehru's role, held together by one idea (friends with both, follower of neither), in small steps with model answers, quick checks, an exam toolkit and a last-minute revision sheet. Follows the ICSE Class 10 syllabus, Chapter 15 (Non-Aligned Movement), in the order of Total History & Civics.

**One idea runs through this whole chapter: friends with both, follower of neither.** In the **Cold War**, newly free nations of Asia and Africa joined **neither** bloc, but still **spoke up** on every issue on its **merits**. Built on **Panchsheel**, launched at **Belgrade (1961)**, led by **Nehru, Tito and Nasser**.

children.label: About this roadmap
children.desc:
**What it is.** A step-by-step path through Chapter 15, *Non-Aligned Movement*, of the History part of the ICSE Class 10 History and Civics syllabus. It follows the order of *Total History & Civics* for Class 10.

**Who it is for.** Class 10 students who find history hard, and want to understand this chapter and score decent marks in it. It also works for revision, and for the teachers and parents helping them: the last milestone is written for adults.

**The one idea.** Friends with both, follower of neither. In the Cold War, newly free nations of Asia and Africa joined neither the US bloc nor the Soviet bloc, but still spoke up on every issue on its merits. Their movement rested on Panchsheel, was launched at Belgrade in 1961, and was led by Nehru, Tito and Nasser.

**How it is different from the textbook.** The textbook mixes meaning, history and Nehru's views. Here one picture, **friends with both, follower of neither**, explains non-alignment, and the favourite exam point (**not neutrality, not isolation, not non-commitment**) gets its own step. Every answer is a **point plus one fact**, with fresh model answers.

**What is inside.**
- 10 milestones and 36 small steps. The 28 solid steps are the core path. The dashed ones are optional.
- 35 practice questions with hidden answers.
- 25 click-to-check questions that say right or wrong, and why: a quick check after each of the 5 main milestones, and a 10-question self-test.
- A **last-minute revision sheet**: every date, key term, name and trap on one page.
- *Start here* fixes the basic skills the chapter needs, and *Check yourself* shows which ones to work on.
- Optional: picture study and two structured challenge questions, and a section for teachers and parents with a 4-period lesson plan, the mistakes to watch for and a 5-minute exit ticket.

**Can you trust it?** Dates, names and places follow the textbook, and the few slips found in it are pointed out gently. A computer program checks that every date sits in the right order and every click-to-check answer is marked right. All the model answers are written fresh, so students still get fresh practice from their textbook. If you spot a mistake, use **Report a problem** at the top of the page.

**Not official.** This is a free, independent resource. It follows the ICSE syllabus but is not made or endorsed by CISCE or by any publisher. It is shared under the **CC BY-SA 4.0** licence: you may copy, adapt and share it, as long as you credit it and share your version the same way.

children.label: Check yourself (2 minutes)
children.desc: Four quick questions. Write your answers first, then open each box. If you get one wrong, do the step named in the answer.

faq.q: 1. Name the three founding fathers of NAM.
faq.a: **Nehru, Tito, Nasser.** Wrong? Do *Who's who in this chapter*.

faq.q: 2. Does non-alignment mean staying silent?
faq.a: **No**: it means not **following** either bloc, while still **speaking up**. Wrong? Do *Two gangs, and the students who joined neither*.

faq.q: 3. What were the two blocs?
faq.a: The **US** bloc and the **Soviet** bloc. Wrong? Do *Two gangs, and the students who joined neither*.

faq.q: 4. How many points for a 2-mark answer?
faq.a: **Two**, each with **one fact**. Wrong? Do *How ICSE asks, and the answer shape*.

children.label: Who's who in this chapter
children.desc:
- **The two power blocs** of the Cold War: the **USA** (capitalist) and the **USSR** (communist).
- **Founding fathers of NAM:** **Jawaharlal Nehru** (India), **Josip Broz Tito** (Yugoslavia), **Gamal Abdel Nasser** (Egypt).
- Also important: **Sukarno** (Indonesia), **Kwame Nkrumah** (Ghana), and China's **Zhou Enlai** at Bandung.
- **Military alliances:** **NATO** and **SEATO** (US side), the **Warsaw Pact** (Soviet side).

faq.q: Your turn: name the three founding fathers of NAM and their countries.
faq.a: **Jawaharlal Nehru** (India), **Josip Broz Tito** (Yugoslavia), **Gamal Abdel Nasser** (Egypt).

children.label: Two gangs, and the students who joined neither
children.desc:
This chapter has **one idea**: **friends with both, follower of neither**.

Picture a school after a big fight. The two strongest students form **two gangs**, and each wants everyone to join.

- Some students, **new** to the school, say: 'We'll be **friendly with both**, but we won't **follow** either.'
- They do **not** stay silent. When something is **wrong**, they say so, whichever gang did it.

After 1945, the two gangs were the **US bloc** and the **Soviet bloc** (the **Cold War**). The new students were the newly free nations of **Asia and Africa**. Their choice was **non-alignment**.

faq.q: Your turn: in the story, are the new students 'neutral'?
faq.a: **No.** They **speak up** on what is right or wrong; they just refuse to **follow** either gang.

children.label: How ICSE asks, and the answer shape
children.desc:
ICSE asks history in three ways.

- **Multiple choice:** 1 mark. Pick one option.
- **Short answer:** usually 2 marks. Write **two points**.
- **Structured question:** parts (a), (b), (c), worth 3 or 4 marks each. Write **one point per mark**.

Each point has **one fact**: a name, a date or a place. A point without a fact looks vague and loses marks.

**Model answer.** *Give two features of non-alignment.*

- It does **not join** either power bloc, and opposes military alliances like **NATO** and the **Warsaw Pact**.
- It takes an **active** part in world affairs, judging each issue **on its merits**.

faq.q: Your turn: what is wrong with this answer? 'It wants peace.'
faq.a: It has **no fact**. Add one: for example, *'It opposes military alliances like NATO and the Warsaw Pact.'*

topics.label: What non-alignment means
topics.desc:
**Goal:** explain the meaning and features of non-alignment, and why it is not neutrality.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, the short-answer and structured questions on the meaning of non-alignment, and Exercise II (structured) question 1(a).

children.label: Meaning and features

faq.q: Your turn: what is meant by non-alignment?
faq.a: A foreign policy of **not joining** either power bloc, while taking an **active** part in world affairs for peace.

children.label: Not neutral, not isolated
children.desc:
Students often confuse non-alignment with three other things. It is **none** of them.

- **Not neutrality:** a neutral country takes **no side** at all. A non-aligned country **takes a stand** on each issue.
- **Not isolation:** it does **not** cut itself off; it takes **full part** in world affairs.
- **Not non-commitment:** it is firmly **committed** to peace, justice and freedom.

**Model answer.** *Explain how non-alignment is not neutrality.*

- A neutral country takes **no side** in disputes.
- A non-aligned country judges each issue **on its merits** and **speaks out** against wrong, whichever bloc does it.

faq.q: Your turn: why is non-alignment not 'isolation'?
faq.a: Non-aligned countries take an **active part** in world affairs; they only refuse to **join a bloc**.

topics.label: Why new nations chose non-alignment
topics.desc:
**Goal:** give the factors that led newly free nations to choose non-alignment.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, the short-answer and structured questions on when and why non-alignment emerged.

children.label: Fear of the Cold War, pride in new freedom
children.desc:
- **Cold War tension:** joining a bloc could drag a country into another **war**, even a **nuclear** one.
- **New freedom:** countries that had just thrown off **colonial** rule did not want to be **controlled** again by a big power.
- **Independent judgement:** they wanted to solve problems **their own way**, without outside pressure.

faq.q: Your turn: when did non-alignment emerge, and why?
faq.a: During the **Cold War**, after the Second World War, because newly free nations did not want to be pulled into **superpower rivalry**.

children.label: Development and a collective voice
children.desc:
- **Friendship with all:** they wanted **goodwill** with every nation, especially in Asia and Africa.
- **Development:** they were **poor** and needed **money and technology**. Staying out of blocs let them take **aid from both sides**, without strings.
- **Collective moral force:** alone they were weak; **together** they could speak up for **peace**.

faq.q: Your turn: how did non-alignment help poor nations develop?
faq.a: They could get **aid and technology** from **both** blocs without having to obey either.

children.label: Quick check: why nations chose it
children.desc:

Wrong? Read the reason, then look back at the step it names.

quiz.q: When did the idea of non-alignment emerge?
options: During the Cold War, after the Second World War
quiz.why: See *Fear of the Cold War, pride in new freedom*.

quiz.q: Why did new nations want to stay out of the blocs?
options: To protect their newly won freedom from big-power pressure
quiz.why: See *Fear of the Cold War, pride in new freedom*.

quiz.q: Why did non-alignment help poor new nations economically?
options: They could take aid and technology from both sides without strings

topics.label: From Panchsheel to Belgrade
topics.desc:
**Goal:** state the five principles of Panchsheel, and trace how NAM was founded.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, the short-answer and structured questions on Panchsheel and the launch of NAM, and Exercise II question 1(b).

children.label: Panchsheel: five principles
children.desc:
In **April 1954**, **India** and **China** signed an agreement based on **five principles** of peaceful co-existence: **Panchsheel**.

- **Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty.**
- **Mutual non-aggression.**
- **Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs.**
- **Equality and mutual benefit.**
- **Peaceful co-existence.**

These became the **guiding principles** of the Non-Aligned Movement.

faq.q: Your turn: state the five principles of Panchsheel.
faq.a: Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty; Mutual non-aggression; Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs; Equality and mutual benefit; Peaceful co-existence.

children.label: Bandung, 1955
children.desc:
- In **April 1955**, **29** countries of **Asia and Africa** met at **Bandung**, Indonesia, hosted by **Sukarno**.
- **Nehru**, China's **Zhou Enlai** and Egypt's **Nasser** were among its leading voices.
- It **condemned colonialism** and called for **economic growth** of the newly free countries.

Bandung **paved the way** for the Non-Aligned Movement.

faq.q: Your turn: what was the importance of the Bandung Conference?
faq.a: It brought newly free nations of **Asia and Africa** together against **colonialism**, and **paved the way** for NAM.

children.label: Belgrade, 1961: the architects
children.desc:
- NAM was **formally launched** at its first summit in **Belgrade**, Yugoslavia, in **September 1961**, with **25** member countries.
- Its **founding fathers**: **Jawaharlal Nehru** (India), **Josip Broz Tito** (Yugoslavia), **Gamal Abdel Nasser** (Egypt). **Sukarno** (Indonesia) and **Kwame Nkrumah** (Ghana) are often counted among the founders too.
- It discussed **Berlin**, the **Congo**, China's seat in the UN and **apartheid** in South Africa.
- It demanded an **end to colonialism** and **complete disarmament**.

Membership grew to about **120** countries by 2012.

faq.q: Your turn: where and when was NAM formally launched?
faq.a: At **Belgrade**, Yugoslavia, in **September 1961**.

topics.label: Objectives and achievements
topics.desc:
**Goal:** state the objectives of NAM, and what it achieved.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, the short-answer and structured questions on the objectives of NAM, Exercise II question 1(c), and Exercise III (picture study).

children.label: Objectives of NAM

faq.q: Your turn: give four objectives of NAM.
faq.a: Oppose **colonialism and racism**; work for **peaceful settlement** of disputes; **abolish nuclear weapons**; **strengthen the UN**.

children.label: What NAM achieved
children.desc:
- It helped **ease tension** between the two blocs.
- It spoke against the **arms race**.
- It supported **peace, justice and freedom**, and the end of **colonial rule**.
- It pushed for a fairer world economy: the first **UNCTAD** (1964) owed much to non-aligned efforts.
- It made rich nations see that the **poverty** of the third world affects **everyone**.

It also had **limits**: it could not stop wars between its own members, like **Iran and Iraq**.

faq.q: Your turn: has NAM achieved its objectives? Give one success and one limit.
faq.a: **Success:** it helped **ease Cold War tension**. **Limit:** it could not stop wars between its own members, like **Iran and Iraq**.

children.label: Quick check: objectives and achievements
children.desc:
Three questions on this milestone. Click an answer to check it.

Wrong? Read the reason, then look back at the step it names.

quiz.q: Which is an objective of NAM?
options: To form a third military bloc
To oppose colonialism, imperialism and racial discrimination
quiz.why: NAM is **not** a third bloc. See *Objectives of NAM*.

quiz.q: What is the NIEO that NAM called for?
options: A New International Economic Order based on equity and justice
A trade bloc against the USA
A new UN agency for weapons

quiz.q: Which is an achievement of NAM?
options: It won the Second World War
It helped ease tension between the two blocs

topics.label: Nehru's role
topics.desc:
**Goal:** explain Jawaharlal Nehru's role in the Non-Aligned Movement.

Practice: in the chapter exercises in *Total History & Civics*, the short-answer and structured questions on Nehru's view and role, and Exercise II question 2.

children.label: Nehru's vision
children.desc:
- **India** was the **first** country to follow non-alignment, under **Nehru**.
- In the **US Congress** (1949) he said India's policy was **not neutralist**: where **freedom** or **justice** was threatened, India would **not** be neutral; it would work actively for **peace**.
- He saw that joining a bloc would put the **freedom** of new nations at risk.
- He said that aligning with one power means **giving up your own opinion** to follow someone else's.

faq.q: Your turn: what was Nehru's view about non-alignment?
faq.a: It was **not neutrality**: India would **not join** a bloc, but would **actively** stand for **freedom, justice and peace**.

children.label: Spokesman of the new nations
children.desc:
- Nehru **led** the countries of Asia and Africa towards non-alignment, and convinced them they had real **moral force** together.
- With **Tito, Nasser, Zhou Enlai, Sukarno** and **Nkrumah**, he made **Bandung** a success.
- He opposed **military pacts** on both sides, like **NATO, SEATO** and the **Warsaw Pact**: they fed the **arms race** and big-power control.
- He favoured **democratic socialism**, not either bloc's system. Non-alignment was meant to protect **freedom of choice**, not to form a third bloc.

faq.q: Your turn: why did Nehru oppose military alliances?
faq.a: He believed they encouraged **imperialism** and an **arms race**, and dragged small nations into **big-power** quarrels.

children.label: Against apartheid and the arms race
children.desc:
- **Apartheid:** India pressed the **UN** to take diplomatic and economic action against **South Africa's** racial discrimination.
- **Colonialism:** India backed the freedom of countries still under **foreign rule**.
- **Arms race:** Nehru called for **disarmament** and an end to nuclear weapons. India signed the **test-ban treaty** of **1963**.

**Model answer.** *What did Nehru do to curb the arms race?*

- He called for **disarmament** and the **abolition of nuclear weapons**.
- India signed the **nuclear test-ban treaty** of **1963**.

links.label: Wikipedia: Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty

faq.q: Your turn: give one way Nehru fought racial discrimination.
faq.a: India pressed the **UN** to act against **apartheid** in **South Africa**.

topics.label: Exam toolkit: words and reasons
topics.desc: **Goal:** collect the easy marks: key terms, answers in the right shape, 'why' questions and dates.

children.label: Key terms to learn word for word
children.desc:
- **Non-alignment:** a foreign policy of not joining either power bloc while taking an active part in world affairs for peace.
- **Power bloc:** a group of countries led by a superpower, the USA or the USSR, in the Cold War.
- **Panchsheel:** the five principles of peaceful co-existence agreed by India and China in 1954.
- **Non-Aligned Movement (NAM):** the group of non-aligned nations formally launched at Belgrade in 1961.
- **NIEO:** a New International Economic Order based on equity, equality and justice.

faq.q: Your turn: cover the list. What is Panchsheel?
faq.a: The **five principles of peaceful co-existence** agreed by **India and China** in **1954**.

children.label: Answers in the right shape
children.desc:
**Short answer (2 marks):** two points, each with **one fact**.

**Structured part (3 or 4 marks):** one point per mark. Start each point on a **new line**. Keep each to **one or two sentences**.

**Model answer.** *State three objectives of the Non-Aligned Movement. (3 marks)*

- To keep newly free nations **away from superpower rivalry** and protect their **freedom**.
- To oppose **colonialism, imperialism and racial discrimination**.
- To work for **disarmament** and the **abolition of nuclear weapons**.

**Three things that lose marks:** saying NAM was launched at **Bandung**; calling non-alignment **neutrality**; listing **Zhou Enlai** as a founding father of NAM.

faq.q: Your turn: write a 2-mark answer. 'Name three founder members of NAM.'
faq.a: **Jawaharlal Nehru** (India), **Josip Broz Tito** (Yugoslavia), **Gamal Abdel Nasser** (Egypt).

children.label: 'Why' questions: model answers
children.desc: Try each one in your notebook before you open it.

faq.q: Why did newly free nations fear joining a bloc?
faq.a: It could drag them into a **war** and put their new **freedom** under a big power's control.

faq.q: Why is NAM not a 'third bloc'?
faq.a: It is **not a military alliance**; it protects each nation's **freedom of choice**.

faq.q: Why did Panchsheel matter to NAM?
faq.a: Its **five principles** of peaceful co-existence became NAM's **guiding principles**.

faq.q: Why did NAM call for an NIEO?
faq.a: Most members were **poor**, and the world economy favoured **rich** nations.

faq.q: Why is Nehru called an architect of NAM?
faq.a: India under Nehru was the **first** to follow non-alignment, and he **led** the new nations towards it.

children.label: Dates to learn
children.desc:
Read it top to bottom. Say each line aloud once.

- **1949:** Nehru's speech in the US Congress.
- **April 1954:** Panchsheel: India and China.
- **April 1955:** Bandung Conference (29 countries).
- **September 1961:** First NAM summit, Belgrade (25 countries).
- **1963:** India signs the nuclear test-ban treaty.
- **1964:** First UNCTAD.
- **2012:** NAM has about 120 members.

faq.q: Your turn: how many years after Panchsheel was NAM launched?

children.label: Picture study: who is this?
children.desc:
The exam may show a **picture** and ask who it is. Then it asks two or three facts. For each person, learn **who** and **two facts**.

- **Nehru, Tito and Nasser together:** the **founding fathers** of NAM; Belgrade, 1961.
- **Nehru with Zhou Enlai:** **Panchsheel** (1954); Bandung.
- **Josip Broz Tito:** **Yugoslavia**; hosted the first summit at **Belgrade**.
- **Gamal Abdel Nasser:** **Egypt**; a founding father.
- **The NAM logo:** the symbol of the movement's summits.

faq.q: Your turn: a picture of Nehru, Tito and Nasser. Name the organisation and where it was formed.
faq.a: The **Non-Aligned Movement**, formed at **Belgrade** in **1961**.

topics.desc: **Goal:** see the whole chapter on one page, then test yourself. Read the sheet the night before the exam and again on the morning.

children.label: Last-minute revision sheet
children.desc:
**The one idea:** **friends with both, follower of neither.** In the **Cold War**, newly free nations of Asia and Africa joined **neither** the US bloc nor the Soviet bloc, but still **spoke up** on every issue on its **merits**. Built on **Panchsheel**, launched at **Belgrade (1961)**, led by **Nehru, Tito and Nasser**.

**Dates to know**
- **1949** Nehru in the US Congress: India will not be neutral where freedom or justice is threatened.
- **April 1954** **Panchsheel** agreed by India and China. **April 1955** **Bandung** Conference (29 Asian and African countries).
- **September 1961** first NAM summit, **Belgrade**, Yugoslavia (25 countries). About **120** members by 2012.

**Key terms**
- **Non-alignment:** a foreign policy of **not joining** either power bloc, while taking an **active** part in world affairs.
- **Power bloc:** a group of countries led by a superpower (USA or USSR).
- **Panchsheel:** the **five principles** of peaceful co-existence.
- **NIEO:** a **New International Economic Order** based on equity and justice.

**Panchsheel**
- **Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty**.
- **Mutual non-aggression**.
- **Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs**.
- **Equality and mutual benefit**.
- **Peaceful co-existence**.

**Key points**
- **Features:** not aligned to any bloc; **against military alliances** (NATO, SEATO, Warsaw Pact); **free** foreign policy; **active** in world affairs; judges issues on **merit**; upholds **freedom and justice**.
- **Not** neutrality (it takes stands), **not** isolation (it takes part), **not** non-commitment (it is committed to peace and justice).
- **Factors:** **Cold War** tension; pride in **new freedom**; right to **independent judgement**; **friendship** with all; need for **aid without strings**; a **collective moral force**.
- **Objectives:** keep away from **superpower rivalry**; protect **new freedom**; oppose **colonialism, imperialism, racism**; **sovereign equality**; **peaceful settlement**; oppose **force** and **nuclear weapons**; strengthen the **UN**; **human rights**; **NIEO**.
- **Achievements:** eased **Cold War** tension; opposed the **arms race**; supported peace and freedom; pushed for **NIEO** and **UNCTAD (1964)**.
- **Nehru:** India **first** to follow non-alignment; **architect** of NAM; spokesman of new nations; against **military pacts**, **apartheid** and the **arms race**; India signed the **test-ban treaty (1963)**.

**Traps:** NAM was **launched at Belgrade (1961)**, not Bandung (1955). Panchsheel was **India and China (1954)**. Non-alignment is **not neutrality**. The three founders: **Nehru (India), Tito (Yugoslavia), Nasser (Egypt)**.

A structured question in three parts. Write your answer first, then open the box.

faq.q: Model answer
faq.a:
(a) It **takes stands** on issues (not neutral); it **takes part** in world affairs (not isolated); it is **committed** to peace and justice (not non-committed).

(b) Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty; Mutual non-aggression; Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs; Equality and mutual benefit; Peaceful co-existence.

(c) Stay away from **superpower rivalry**; oppose **colonialism and racism**; **peaceful settlement** of disputes; **abolish nuclear weapons**.

children.label: Structured question: Nehru's role
children.desc:
A structured question in three parts. Write your answer first, then open the box.

- (a) His vision in starting NAM. (3 marks)
- (b) Curbing the arms race. (3 marks)
- (c) As spokesman of the new nations of Asia and Africa. (4 marks)

faq.q: Model answer
faq.a:
(a) He saw that joining a bloc would **endanger the freedom** of new nations; India would stay out of blocs but **actively** work for peace.

(b) He called for **disarmament** and an end to nuclear weapons; India signed the **test-ban treaty** (1963).

(c) He **led** them towards non-alignment, made **Bandung** a success, opposed **military pacts**, and pressed the UN against **apartheid** and **colonialism**.

topics.label: For teachers and parents
topics.desc:
**For the adults helping.** Students can skip this milestone.

The syllabus asks for the brief meaning of non-alignment, its objectives, Panchsheel, the role of Jawaharlal Nehru and the names of the architects of NAM.

children.label: How to help a student who is struggling
children.desc:
- Start with the **two gangs** story; students grasp 'friends with both, follower of neither' quickly.
- Write **NOT neutral, NOT isolated, NOT non-committed** on the board; it answers a favourite exam question.
- Learn Panchsheel with a **hand**: five fingers, five principles.
- Mark **Bandung** (1955) and **Belgrade** (1961) on a map; keep them apart.
- Ask: 'Is NAM still useful today?' Let students discuss.
- Insist on **one fact per point**.

children.label: A 4-period plan, with activities
children.desc:
- **Period 1:** Two gangs; meaning, features, not neutral. Exercise I.
- **Period 2:** Factors; Panchsheel; Bandung; Belgrade and the architects.
- **Period 3:** Objectives and achievements; Nehru's role. Exercise II.
- **Period 4:** Revision sheet, self-test, exit ticket; picture study.

children.label: Mistakes to watch for
children.desc:
- Calling non-alignment **neutrality**.
- Saying NAM was launched at **Bandung**.
- Saying Panchsheel was signed with **Pakistan**.
- Missing one of the **five** Panchsheel principles.
- Naming **Zhou Enlai** as a NAM founder.
- Calling NAM a **military bloc**.

children.label: Exit ticket (5 minutes)
children.desc: Five short questions covering the main ideas. The answers are below.

faq.q: 1. What is non-alignment?
faq.a: Not joining **either bloc**, while taking an **active** part in world affairs.

faq.q: 2. Name two principles of Panchsheel.
faq.a: **Mutual non-aggression** and **peaceful co-existence**.

faq.q: 3. Where and when was NAM launched?
4. Name the three founding fathers.
faq.a: **Jawaharlal Nehru** (India), **Josip Broz Tito** (Yugoslavia), **Gamal Abdel Nasser** (Egypt).

faq.q: 5. Give one objective of NAM.
faq.a: To oppose **colonialism and racial discrimination**.
